text: Final categorization: OK (Justification: The paper presents a non-review, applied research study using the GIS-based Land Use Scanner model to simulate future land use across the entire Netherlands (national-scale spatial implementation). The primary objective is residential land use prediction under three distinct, internally consistent future scenarios (Divided Europe, European Co-ordination, Global Competition), enabling quantitative comparison of outcomes. The modeling approach is spatially explicit, grid-based (500m resolution), and produces mapped LULC projections for 2020. Although accuracy metrics like Kappa or overall accuracy are not reported, the paper provides quantitative change rates (e.g., hectares converted, dwelling counts, land demand by sector) and validates model parameters against observed 1980–1995 trends. Residential construction—a single but central LULC class—is explicitly modeled as the driver of land use change, satisfying inclusion criteria. The study does not fall under any exclusion criteria: it is national in scope, includes multiple future scenarios, generates spatially explicit LULC outputs, and focuses on land use prediction rather than being purely economic, ecological, or methodological without application.)
